theater: 幼發拉底河中游巴比倫與蘇薩之間

battle.name: 埃蘭對巴比倫的進攻
battle.theater: 幼發拉底河中游巴比倫與蘇薩之間
battle.brief: 前1770年，蘇薩的埃蘭王國沿幼發拉底河谷深入巴比倫尼尼微，攻城掠廟，戰事在城牆與城郊之間反覆；巴比倫靠城防與列陣的長矛守住廟產，埃蘭沒有取得長期佔領。卡面的埃及長矛正屬同一世代的武備：套筒銅矛頭安在木杆上，是當年兩河與埃及步兵共有的骨架兵器。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方是埃蘭王國與巴比倫城邦，時間落在古巴比倫時代的前段，約前十八世紀末至前十七世紀初，戰場在美索不達米亞中游、幼發拉底河兩側的谷地，以及巴比倫尼尼微的城牆之外。埃蘭一方以伊朗西南胡齊斯坦平原的蘇薩為中心，王室是自阿卡德時代以來控制蘇薩的埃蘭王族，宮廷與神廟系統以伊什胡爾拉與伊南舒里寧女神的神廟為核心，軍隊以王室直屬的步兵與弓手為骨幹，配以輕型雙輪車隊與數量不多的乘騎，攻城依靠土壘、斜坡與撞槌，並且習慣以分隊掠奪的方式取得穀物、牲畜與神像作為戰利品。巴比倫一方是阿摩利特王朝的巴比倫王國，國王同時是最高軍事統帥，軍隊由王室常備兵與各城邦、神廟按比例抽丁組成的民兵合成，步兵持矛與斧列陣，弓手列於陣前或兩翼，車隊負責追擊與傳令，另有河上船隊負責監視幼發拉底與運糧。巴比倫城牆是這一方的底牌：內城牆周長約八公里、外城牆約十八公里，沿牆有數百座塔樓，城外有引水渠與濠溝，護城河直接取自幼發拉底。當時周邊還有埃什努那、拉爾薩、馬里、亞述等城邦，馬里王宮的文書顯示埃蘭的軍隊與使者出現在希帕一帶，說明這場衝突從一開始就是幼發拉底河谷體系內的角力，而不是孤立的邊境摩擦。埃及在此時處於第二中間期與第十七王朝之交，與兩河的直接聯繫多經由黎凡特商路，因此卡面這件埃及長矛並非戰場上的繳獲物，而是與巴比倫、埃蘭共享的同代步兵兵器形制。
countriesEn: The belligerents in this war were the kingdom of Elam and the city-state of Babylon, the fighting falling in the early part of the Old Babylonian period, roughly the end of the eighteenth to the beginning of the seventeenth century BC, in the middle Euphrates valley of Mesopotamia, around the walls of Babylon. On the Elamite side the centre was Susa on the Khuzestan plain of south-western Iran. The royal house was the Elamite dynasty that had held Susa since the Akkadian period, and the court and temple system turned on the sanctuaries of the goddesses Ishhurra and Inshushinak. The army was built on the royal household infantry and archers, with light two-wheeled chariots and a limited number of riders, and siege work was done with earthworks, ramps and battering rams; the Elamites were also accustomed to take grain, livestock and statues of the gods as spoil. On the Babylonian side stood the Babylonia of the Amorite dynasty, where the king was at once the supreme commander: the field army combined a standing royal force with militia levied in fixed proportions from the towns and the temples, infantry standing in line with spears and axes, archers posted in front or on the flanks, chariots used for pursuit and for carrying messages, and river craft patrolling the Euphrates and carrying grain. The city wall was the trump card on that side: the inner wall ran about eight kilometres and the outer wall about eighteen, with several hundred towers along them, and outside the walls an irrigation canal and a ditch drew their water directly from the Euphrates. Around them in the same period stood Eshnunna, Larsa, Mari and Assyria, and the archives of Mari show Elamite troops and envoys operating around Sippar, which means this was a struggle inside the Euphrates system from the start and not an isolated frontier incident. Egypt at the time lay at the meeting of the Second Intermediate Period and the Seventeenth Dynasty, and its direct links with Mesopotamia ran largely through the Levantine trade; the Egyptian spear on the card is therefore not a captured object from the battlefield but a form of infantry weapon shared by Babylonia, Elam and Egypt alike.
people: 能確定的名字不多，而且分屬兩個系統。巴比倫方面，這場戰爭落在漢摩拉比統治的前後，按中等年表其統治約在前1792至前1750年，其父辛美里阿布與母后蘇姆尼圖在宮廷文獻中留下了痕跡；漢摩拉比早期的《致父王書》以流暢的書記體敘述自己的征伐，與他晚年的《法典》序言一樣，把自己描寫成從海濱之國打到胡齊斯坦的埃蘭的君主。序言還提到他沿波斯灣一側、面向埃蘭築起一道城牆，並在卡西提利亞什設防，這道防線的具體位置至今有不同說法，但可以確定它與防範埃蘭有關。埃蘭方面，蘇薩的王表在古巴比倫時代可以排出大致輪廓：圖爾塔庫、伊丁-西穆魯姆、庫克-西穆特、提普塔克齊等名字先後在位，但究竟哪一位率軍深入巴比倫尼尼微，學界仍只能靠編年史的敘述與年表的推算去對應，多數說法把這次進攻繫於提普塔克齊一系，另有學者認為年代要更晚，落在卡西特人上台前後。人物群體方面，巴比倫一端有編寫編年史的書吏、埃薩吉拉與埃庫爾的神廟管理員、編訂王表的祭司，以及被徵召的城邦民兵；埃蘭一端有蘇薩宮廷的官員與神廟人員，以及被文獻提到在希帕一線指揮軍隊的埃蘭將領。馬里王宮的檔案還留下同期人物的名字：王基馬利在位於前1775至前1761年，與這場戰爭幾乎重疊，他的宮廷同時接待巴比倫與埃蘭的使節，也記下兩邊使者之間的威脅語。此外還要記住一位死於戰場之外的埃蘭君主：沙瑪斯阿杜一世的勝利石碑今日出土於蘇薩，那是阿摩利特人自己的凱旋碑，卻被埃蘭人帶回高原收藏，它說明兩個王朝的戰爭從來是在彼此的首都之間搬家。
peopleEn: Few names can be established, and they belong to two different systems. On the Babylonian side the war falls in the time of Hammurabi, who under the middle chronology ruled from about 1792 to 1750 BC; his father Sin-Muballit and his mother Sumu-nitum left traces in the court literature. The Letter to His Father from Hammurabi's early years describes his campaigns in a flowing scribal style, and like the prologue of his later Code it presents him as a ruler who fought from the lands by the sea to Elam in Khuzestan. The prologue further mentions that he built a wall along the side of the Persian Gulf facing Elam and set up a fortified position at Kashtiliash; the exact position of that line is still disputed, but what is certain is that it belonged to his defence against Elam. On the Elamite side the king list of Susa can be set out in rough outline for the Old Babylonian period: names such as Turtakku, Iddin-Simurrum, Kuk-Simut and Tiptakzi succeed one another on the throne, but which of them led an army deep into Babylonia can still only be worked out from the narrative of the chronicles and from calculations on the chronology; most accounts attach the raid to the line of Tiptakzi, while others put it later, around the time the Kassites took the throne. As for groups of people: on the Babylonian side the scribes who compiled the chronicles, the administrators of the temples of Esagila and Ekur, the priests who drew up the king list, and the militia levied from the towns; on the Elamite side the officials and temple personnel of the court at Susa, and the Elamite commanders whom the documents place in the field around Sippar. The archives of Mari preserve the names of contemporaries: Zimri-Lim reigned from about 1775 to 1761 BC, almost exactly overlapping this war, and his court received envoys from both Babylon and Elam and recorded the threatening language exchanged between them. One more figure deserves to be remembered, an Elamite king who did not die on the field: the victory stele of Samshi-Adad I is excavated today at Susa. It is an Amorite triumph monument that the Elamites carried back to the highlands and kept, and it shows that the wars between the two houses always ended up moving monuments from one capital to the other.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛是早王朝時期的形制：銅或青銅的矛頭做成中空套管，套在木杆前端再加以固定，整支長矛的高度與埃及人舉矛的姿勢相配，矛尖在最遠處，可以用來格擋。埃及人先用它守城垣，後來用它收復失地；到古巴比倫時代，這個形制在整個近東幾乎沒有改變，巴比倫與埃蘭的步兵用的正是同一類套筒長矛。銅與青銅仍是兵器主料，鐵在這個時期屬罕見材質，只出現在少量刀、匕首與飾件上。弓是木胎角飾的複合弓，箭鏃為銅或青銅，埃及方面則流行內凹的埃及式弓；斧有套筒式的銅斧，砍伐與近身格鬥兩用，埃及另有短柄的直角柄斧；盾以蒙皮圓盾為主，也有可以立在地上遮蔽全身的高盾。運輸與機動靠馬：雙輪輕車以兩匹或四匹馬牽引，舊巴比倫時期馬里王宮的文書把車隊編制寫得很細，步兵以車為快速機動與衝鋒手段；攻城則靠斜坡、土壘、撞槌與挖掘，城頭有投擲陶球與石塊的火力。城防方面，這一時期的巴比倫城牆仍是土坯核心加燒磚貼面，不是今日所見的釉面磚版本，伊斯塔爾門與彩釉城牆是六百年後新巴比倫時代的東西，與這場戰爭無關。皮製箭袋與盾套、車上的箭桶、繫在腰帶上的短斧與匕首，構成了士兵隨身裝備的最小單位；在編年史的語彙裡，這場戰爭留下的最常見裝備名目，仍然是矛、弓、斧、盾與車。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is a form that goes back to the Early Dynastic period: the copper or bronze head is made as a hollow socket, slipped over the front of a wooden shaft and then secured, and the whole weapon matches the height at which an Egyptian carried a spear, with the point at the furthest reach so that it could also be used to ward blows off. The Egyptians used it first to hold city walls and later to recover lost territory; by the Old Babylonian period the form had changed very little anywhere in the Near East, and the infantry of Babylon and of Elam carried spears of exactly the same socketed type. Copper and bronze were still the principal materials of arms, iron being a rarity in this period and appearing only in a few blades, daggers and fittings. The bow was a composite of wood with horn fittings, its arrowheads of copper or bronze, while Egypt favoured the inward-curving Egyptian bow; the axe was a socketed copper axe serving both for work and for close combat, and Egypt also had the short-hafted axe set at a right angle; shields were mostly round and covered with hide, though tall shields that could be set on the ground to cover the whole body also existed. Transport and manoeuvre rested on the horse: light two-wheeled chariots drawn by two or four horses, with the composition of the chariot corps written down in fine detail in the court archives of Mari, infantry using the chariot for speed and for the charge; siege work relied on ramps, earthworks, battering rams and excavation, with the walls hurling clay balls and stones. On the fortification side, the Babylon wall of this period was still a mud-brick core faced with fired brick, not the glazed-brick version seen today: the Ishtar Gate and the coloured revetment belong to the Neo-Babylonian age six centuries later and have nothing to do with this war. Hide quivers and shield covers, the arrow buckets carried on the chariot, and the short axe and dagger hung at the belt made up the smallest unit of a soldier's personal kit; and in the vocabulary of the chronicles the most commonly listed equipment of this war remains the spear, the bow, the axe, the shield and the chariot.
tactics: 巴比倫與埃蘭的作戰方式都可以從更早的兩河流域傳統推想，但這場衝突有它自己的地理邏輯。巴比倫城坐落在幼發拉底河中游，河道既是屏障也是最短的補給線；埃蘭的遠征隊伍從蘇薩沿克爾克河與胡齊斯坦山麓北上，逆流而上，多在春汛之後、收割之前出動，目標是巴比倫尼尼微周邊的穀物產區、蓄水池與神廟財產，奪走小麥、大麥、椰棗與牲畜，掠奪之外還要取得神像作為戰利品，這在兩河流域是公認的合法所得。防禦的一方因此採守城為本、出城殲敵為輔：先把渡口與灌溉渠上的橋樑控制住，用船隊巡弋幼發拉底，再在城外開闊地與來犯之師接戰；城牆上的弓手居高臨下覆蓋接近路線，車隊用於封閉缺口，步兵在缺口打開時以長矛列陣推進。攻方埃蘭的戰術則是分隊掠奪與集中決戰的混合：輕裝縱隊快速推進，以弓手消耗守軍，待援兵與車隊集結後再作決定性衝擊，或者根本不打會戰，只把戰利品運回蘇薩，以兩河流域的糧食與交通條件看，後者常是更划算的選擇。攻城若成，埃蘭人依靠斜坡與撞槌，而不是長期的圍城；巴比倫人的反擊則以小股游擊隊襲擊埃蘭縱隊的補給線與返程隊伍。總的說，這是一場以城牆為中心、以穀物與神像為爭點的邊境戰，而不是兩軍在開闊地會戰。
tacticsEn: The ways of fighting of Babylon and of Elam can both be reasoned from older Mesopotamian tradition, but this conflict has a geography of its own. Babylon sits on the middle Euphrates, and the river is at once a barrier and the shortest line of supply. The Elamite columns came up from Susa along the Karun and the foothills of Khuzestan, moving against the current, and habitually set out after the spring flood but before the harvest, with the grain districts, the reservoirs and the temple estates around Babylonia as their object: they took wheat, barley, dates and livestock, and beyond plain plunder they wanted the statues of the gods, which in Mesopotamia were recognised as legitimate spoil. The defence therefore worked city-first with a counterstroke in the open: control the fords and the bridges over the irrigation canals first, patrol the Euphrates with river craft, and then meet the invader in the open ground outside the walls; archers on the wall covered the approaches from above, chariots were used to close a breach, and infantry advanced in line with spears once a gap had opened. The Elamite method mixed dispersed plunder with a concentrated decision: light columns pushing fast, archers wearing down the defenders, and a decisive charge once reinforcements and chariots had joined, or no battle at all, taking the loot back to Susa, which in a land where grain and transport were the binding constraint was often the cheaper choice. If the siege was pressed, the Elamites worked with ramps and battering rams rather than a long blockade; the Babylonian counterstroke took the form of small raiding parties striking at the supply line of the Elamite columns and at their return march. In sum this was a frontier war centred on the city wall, fought for grain and statues, rather than a set-piece battle fought in the open.
data: 能核對的數字分三類。第一類是年表：中文的戰爭列表把此役繫於公元前1770年；古巴比倫時代的中等年表與短年表相差約五十年，漢摩拉比在中等年表下統治約前1792至前1750年，在短年表下則是前1848至前1806年，因此同一場衝突的絕對年份會隨年表而移動；中巴比倫編年史一系的文本把埃蘭的入侵放在阿摩利特王朝末段，與卡西特人建國的年份連續推算，卻沒有留下任何明確的年號。第二類是距離與地理：巴比倫城至蘇薩直線約三百七十公里，沿幼發拉底與胡齊斯坦山麓走約五百公里；巴比倫至西帕爾約六十公里，至尼普爾約一百六十公里，至烏爾約二百二十公里，埃蘭遠征隊伍實際要走的正是這條河谷路線；巴比倫內城牆周長約八公里、外城牆約十八公里，牆上有數百座塔樓，城外護城河直接取自幼發拉底。第三類是規模與物質：巴比倫的內外兩重城牆把守軍分在數個區段，馬里王宮的文書顯示同期的軍隊編制以小隊為單位、由車隊與步兵配合，車隊常以三輛或四輛為一隊，但關於這場戰爭的具體兵員數，雙方都沒有留下任何數字；銅是兵器主料，來源在安納托利亞與伊朗高原的礦區，錫在兩河流域極為罕見；冶金整體仍處於銅青銅時代，鐵要到亞述統治晚期才逐漸普及。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is chronology: the Chinese list of battles ties this war to 1770 BC. The middle and short chronologies for the Old Babylonian period differ by about fifty years, so that Hammurabi's reign is about 1792 to 1750 BC in the middle chronology and 1848 to 1806 BC in the short one, and the absolute date of the same clash therefore moves with the chronology chosen. The texts of the Middle Babylonian chronicle family place the Elamite incursion in the last part of the Amorite dynasty, working forward by continuous reckoning from the year the Kassites founded themselves, yet they leave no explicit year behind. The second class is distance and geography: about three hundred and seventy kilometres in a straight line from Babylon to Susa, roughly five hundred by the Euphrates and the foothills of Khuzestan; about sixty kilometres from Babylon to Sippar, about a hundred and sixty to Nippur, about two hundred and twenty to Ur, and the Elamite columns marched exactly this river route. The inner wall of Babylon ran about eight kilometres and the outer wall about eighteen, with several hundred towers, and the moat outside the city drew its water directly from the Euphrates. The third class is scale and material: Babylon's two rings of wall divided the garrison into several sectors, and the court archives of Mari show the military organisation of the period working in small detachments of chariots and infantry together, chariot troops being grouped in three or four vehicles, but no document from either side gives any figure for the numbers engaged in this war. Copper was the principal material of arms, coming from the mining districts of Anatolia and of the Iranian highlands, while tin was extremely scarce in Mesopotamia; metallurgy as a whole still belonged to the copper-and-bronze age, and iron only spread gradually from the later Assyrian period.
cause: 打起來的根由有四層。最遠的一層是結構性的：埃蘭是伊朗高原上的農業王國，蘇薩宮廷與神廟的開支長期高於胡齊斯坦本地能提供的產出，穀物、椰棗、銅料與人口都得從低地的美索不達米亞輸入，而巴比倫尼尼微是這條補給線上最富庶、廟產最集中的一個目標。第二層是地理的：幼發拉底下游的轉運與阿拉伯海的商路由蘇薩與巴比倫共同分享，誰控制河谷中游的橋樑與渡口，誰就控制這條線；兩河流域的傳統又把取得神像視為合法戰利品，掠奪的誘因因此不只在財富。第三層是外交的：巴比倫在這一時期四面受敵，北方有亞述，東方有埃蘭，西北方有馬里與埃什努那，任何一方的牽制都會被對手利用；漢摩拉比自己在波斯灣一側修築面向埃蘭的城牆，正說明他清楚這條戰線的方向。第四層是季節的：兩河流域的農業社會在春汛與夏收之間有一段最脆弱的窗口，糧食還在田裡、軍隊正在遠離基地，掠奪的收益最高而守方的反應最慢。直接導火線沒有留下記載；較合理的推測是某一年春季，埃蘭的遠征隊伍深入巴比倫腹地，奪走大批穀物並擄走神像或工匠，巴比倫王於是點集城邦民兵與王室軍隊，在河谷走廊上迎擊或者北上反擊，戰事就這樣展開。
causeEn: The reasons for the fighting have four layers. The most distant is structural: Elam was an agrarian kingdom on the Iranian plateau, and the expenses of the court and the temples at Susa long exceeded what Khuzestan itself could produce, so grain, dates, copper and people all had to come up from lowland Mesopotamia, and Babylon on the Euphrates was the richest and most treasure-laden target on that supply line. The second layer is geographical: the downriver transshipment and the trade of the Arabian Gulf were shared between Susa and Babylon, and whoever held the bridges and fords of the middle valley held the line; and since Mesopotamian tradition recognised the taking of statues as legitimate spoil, the motive for a raid lay in more than money. The third layer is diplomatic: Babylonia was surrounded by rivals in this period, with Assyria to the north, Elam to the east, Mari and Eshnunna to the north-west, and the distraction of one side was always exploited by another; that Hammurabi himself built a wall facing Elam on the side of the Persian Gulf shows that he knew exactly where that front lay. The fourth layer is seasonal: between the spring flood and the summer harvest the agricultural society of Mesopotamia passed through its most vulnerable window, with the grain still standing in the fields and the armies away from their bases, so that the yield of a raid was highest while the defence was slowest to answer. No record of the immediate occasion survives. The likeliest reconstruction is that in some spring an Elamite column pushed deep into the Babylonian interior, carrying off grain and taking gods or craftsmen, and that the king then called out the militia of the towns together with the royal troops and either met the invaders in the valley corridor or marched north to meet them, and that is how the war was fought.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果沒有留下清晰的記錄，影響只能從前後的格局去讀。短期看，巴比倫尼尼微沒有因此易主：古巴比倫王國在這之後仍延續了一百多年，漢摩拉比的王位傳到其子薩姆希努曼，直到前1595年或短年表下的前1531年才被赫梯王穆爾西里一世洗劫；這說明前1770年前後的埃蘭入侵沒有改變幼發拉底河谷的權力結構。長期看，這場衝突是巴比倫與埃蘭三百年爭奪中的一環：蘇薩在古巴比倫之後沉寂了大約三百年，直到前1155年圖舒魯克-納洪特一世才再度率軍進入巴比倫尼尼微、擄走瑪爾杜克神像，把巴比倫人對埃蘭的恐懼變成一段很長的記憶。另一層影響在編纂與制度：巴比倫的書吏把這類事寫進編年史，把國王與神廟的關係寫進王表與契約，把戰役的規模寫成可以反覆引用的清單；正是這些泥板，讓一場沒有戰報的衝突在三千多年後仍能被指出大致的位置與年代。軍備層面的後果是延續而非變革：銅矛、複合弓、套筒斧與輕車仍是步兵與車隊的骨架，戰車在舊巴比倫末期逐漸讓位給乘騎與馢運，而埃及那支早王朝的長矛傳統在埃及與黎凡特延續得更久，直到青銅與鐵的矛頭先後取代銅質，長矛始終是兩軍列陣時的第一道骨架。
impactEn: The direct consequences of this war left no clear trace, and its effects can only be read from the pattern before and after. In the short term Babylon did not change hands: the Old Babylonian kingdom continued for more than a century afterwards, Hammurabi's throne passing to his son Samsu-nunan, and the city was not to be sacked until 1595 BC, or 1531 BC in the short chronology, when the Hittite king Mursilis I took it. That tells us the Elamite incursion of around 1770 BC did not alter the balance of power in the Euphrates valley. In the longer term the war is one episode in three centuries of contention between Babylon and Elam: Susa went quiet for roughly three centuries after the Old Babylonian period, and only in 1155 BC did Shutruk-Nahhunte I march into Babylonia again and carry off the statue of Marduk, turning the Babylonian fear of Elam into a long memory. A second layer of effect lies in compilation and institutions: Babylonian scribes wrote such events into the chronicles, wrote the relation of king and temple into the king lists and the contracts, and wrote the scale of the fighting into inventories that could be quoted again and again; it is precisely these clay tablets that allow a clash with no battle report to be placed roughly in space and time more than three millennia later. At the level of armament the consequence is continuity rather than change: the copper spear, the composite bow, the socketed axe and the light chariot remained the framework of both infantry and chariot corps, the chariot gave way gradually to riding and to pack animals in the late Old Babylonian period, and the Early Dynastic spear tradition of Egypt lasted longer still in Egypt and the Levant, where bronze and then iron heads in turn replaced copper, the spear remaining the first framework of the line in either army.
result: 勝負與細節都難以還原，必須先把話說在前面。巴比倫方面的年表有長段缺頁，埃蘭的記錄散佚在蘇薩的殘簡與後世引用裡，這一場戰爭沒有留下任何一份雙方的戰報；具體的戰鬥序列、雙方出兵的數目、是否真的在城下列過陣，都只能從結局與制度去反推。可以確定的結局有幾條：第一，巴比倫城沒有因此陷落，古巴比倫王國的統治沒有中斷，後來仍舊存在了近百五十年，直到赫梯人的入侵才改寫城市的命運；第二，埃蘭沒有取得對美索不達米亞的長期佔有，它的南下在巴比倫尼尼微的城牆前停住，之後三百年在兩河史料裡都只是模糊的影子，直到前1155年才真正捲土重來；第三，這次衝突的痕跡落到了文字裡，被記在編年史與王表的抄本中，留在後世學者用來排列年表的紙面上。就過程而言，最可能的輪廓是：埃蘭一方以分隊掠奪為主，試圖在巴比倫防禦薄弱處奪取穀物與神像，必要時在城外集結車隊作一次決定性衝擊；巴比倫一方以守城與反擊相配合，用河運與游擊拖住埃蘭縱隊，同時保住城牆與神廟，最終讓這場戰爭以掠奪得手而佔領未成的方式收場。這種不求一戰定勝負、以消耗換退場的格局，與巴比倫在亞述壓力下最終能撐住的同一套辦法，是同一條河谷的產物。
resultEn: Neither the outcome nor the detail can be reconstructed, and that has to be said at the start. The Babylonian annals have long missing stretches, and the Elamite record survives only in fragments from Susa and in later quotation, so that this war left no battle report from either side. The order of the fighting, the numbers engaged on each side and whether the two armies ever even deployed outside the walls can only be reasoned backwards from the end and from the institutions. Several things about the outcome can be stated with confidence. First, Babylon did not fall as a result of it: the rule of the Old Babylonian kingdom was not interrupted, the city went on existing for close to a century and a half afterwards, and only the incoming of the Hittites changed its destiny. Second, Elam did not obtain a lasting hold on Mesopotamia; its push north stopped at the walls of Babylon, and for the next three centuries it remains only a shadow in the Mesopotamian record, until it really came back in 1155 BC. Third, the mark of the conflict was left in writing, in copies of the chronicles and king lists, on the pages where later scholars arrange their chronology. As for the process, the likeliest outline is this: on the Elamite side the method was dispersed plunder, an attempt to seize grain and gods wherever Babylonian defence was thin, with the chariots massed outside the city for one decisive charge if it should come to that; on the Babylonian side, city defence and counterstroke were combined, using river transport and raiding parties to hold up the Elamite columns while the walls and the temples were kept, so that the war ended with the plunder taken and the occupation not achieved. That pattern, trading a decisive battle for attrition in the hope of driving the enemy off, is the same device by which Babylon was later able to hold out under Assyrian pressure, and it was the product of one and the same river valley.
